questions.stem: The Bhakti movement in South India was started by which two groups of devotional saints (7th-9th C CE)?
questions.explanation: Alvars — 12 Vaishnava devotional poets — composed Tamil hymns to Vishnu (compiled as 'Nalayira Divya Prabandham', 4000 verses). Includes Nammalvar, Andal (only female Alvar — author of Tiruppavai). Nayanars — 63 Shaivite saints, Tamil hymns to Shiva (compiled as 'Tevaram'). Includes Sambandar, Appar, Sundarar (the 'Trimurti'), Manikkavachakar (Tiruvachakam). 9th-10th C philosophical schools — Ramanuja (Vishishtadvaita), Madhva (Dvaita), Vallabha (Shuddhadvaita) — synthesised these strands.

questions.stem: Kabir, the 15th-century mystic-poet, was a disciple of:
questions.explanation: Kabir (~1398-1518) — born to Muslim weaver family in Varanasi. Pupil of Ramananda — a Vaishnava saint who broke caste barriers. Kabir's verses (dohas / sakhis) attack ritualism, idolatry, caste, religious orthodoxy. His compositions appear in the Guru Granth Sahib (~292 padas), in Bijak (Kabir-panth scripture), and in Ramaini, Sabad. Mirabai, Surdas, Nanak were his contemporaries. Tradition says when Kabir died in Maghar, both Hindus and Muslims claimed his body — only flowers were found under the cloth. 'Kabir Jayanti' celebrated.

questions.stem: Guru Nanak Dev (1469-1539), founder of Sikhism, was born at:
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak — born 15 April 1469 (Kartik Purnima celebrated traditionally) at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib, Punjab, Pakistan). First of the 10 Sikh Gurus. Travelled extensively — Mecca, Baghdad, Sri Lanka, Tibet — known as 'Udasis'. Settled at Kartarpur (also in Pakistan) in his last years. Died 22 September 1539. Teachings — Ik Onkar (One God), opposition to caste, equality of all, langar (community kitchen). Compositions: Japji Sahib, Asa-di-Var. Sikh-pilgrim Kartarpur Corridor opened in 2019 lets Indian Sikhs visit without visa.

questions.stem: Mirabai — 16th-century Krishna-devotee saint who composed thousands of bhajans — belonged to which dynasty by birth?

options.option_text: Rathores of Mewar (married into Sisodia royal family)

questions.explanation: Mirabai (1498-1547) — born princess in Rathore family (Merta, Rajasthan). Married Bhojraj, son of Maharana Sanga of Mewar. After her husband's death (1521 at Khanwa), faced persecution from Rana Vikramaditya. Devoted entire life to Krishna; her bhajans in Brij/Rajasthani ('Mere to Giridhar Gopal', 'Payoji Maine Ram Ratan Dhan Payo') are still sung. Travelled to Vrindavan (met Roop Goswami there), then Dwarka. Some legends say she merged with Krishna's idol at Dwarka.

questions.stem: The Maharashtrian Bhakti tradition is associated with which group of poet-saints?

options.option_text: Varkari saints — Jnaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath, Tukaram

questions.explanation: Varkari Sampradaya — devotees of Vithoba (Vitthal) of Pandharpur. Lineage: Jnaneshwar (Dnyaneshwar, 1275-96 — wrote Bhavarthadeepika / Jnaneshwari, Marathi commentary on Bhagavad Gita), Namdev (1270-1350), Eknath (1533-99), Tukaram (1608-50, abhangas — short devotional verses). Annual pilgrimage 'Vari' from Alandi/Dehu to Pandharpur — millions of pilgrims walk each year for Ashadhi Ekadashi. Tukaram's abhangas — 'Vrkshavalli Amha Soyari' — a paean to nature.

questions.stem: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (1486-1534) — founder of Gaudiya Vaishnavism — preached the 'Hare Krishna' mantra and was born in:
questions.explanation: Chaitanya — Vaishnav saint; born Nabadwip, Bengal, 18 February 1486. Originally Vishvambhar Mishra; took sannyasa, became Chaitanya. Spent last 24 years at Puri (Jagannath Temple). Popularised Krishna-bhakti through Sankirtana — congregational chanting of 'Hare Krishna' mantra. Considered an avatar of Krishna by his followers. Founded Gaudiya Vaishnavism — eventually inspired ISKCON (1966 NY, by A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada). Six Goswamis of Vrindavan (Rupa, Sanatana, Jiva, Gopal Bhatta, Raghunatha Bhatta, Raghunath Das) systematised the theology.

questions.stem: Match the saint with their associated language / region — which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Basavanna (1131-67) — founder of the Lingayat / Veerashaiva movement — wrote in KANNADA, not Tamil. Karnataka's social reformer; rejected caste, established 'Anubhava Mantapa' for spiritual debate at Kalyana. His Vachanas (sayings) are core Lingayat literature. Tulsidas (1532-1623) — author of Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi. Surdas (1478-1583) — blind Krishna-poet in Brij Bhasha (Sursagar). Shankaradeva (1449-1568) — Assam Bhakti pioneer; founded Ekasarana Dharma; works in Brajavali (a literary form mixing Brajbhasha + Assamese).
